item.title: Building set ablaze and more than 1,200 arrested as police clash with protesters across France
item.author: Kim Willsher in Paris and William Christou
item.content:encoded: Police fire teargas in Paris and Limoges town hall ‘largely lost’ to fire – with officials blaming violence on ‘ultra-left’More than 1,200 people were arrested in France on Saturday after protesters supporting high school students clashed with police, with some demonstrations later spiralling out of control as buildings were set ablaze and shops looted.Police fired teargas in confrontations with protesters, as demonstrations across France were boosted by other groups angry about high prices and the fraying of a social welfare system.While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully in street marches in scores of cities, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers.Continue reading...

item.title: Ebike rider, 13, charged with sexual touching after girls and women allegedly harassed on northern beaches trails
item.author: Penry Buckley
item.content:encoded: Sydney teenager charged with offensive behaviour and sexual touching without consent in relation to incidents involving females aged 13 to 54An ebike riding 13-year-old boy has been charged with multiple sexual offences allegedly committed against women on walking trails on Sydney’s northern beaches.New South Wales police said the boy was arrested on Saturday evening after a strike force was established to investigate inappropriate comments and alleged sexual touching incidents on walking trails in the Narrabeen area in the first weeks of October.Continue reading...

item.title: Trump Offers Putin Economic Relief in Hopes That Russia Will Return the Favor
item.author: Alan Rappeport
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration is ignoring the will of Congress and waiving new Russia sanctions amid fears that high energy prices will cost Republicans in next month’s elections.

item.title: Arizona joins Nevada to fight proposed cuts to their shares of Colorado River
item.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
item.content:encoded: Move comes after Trump administration announced restrictions that could slash water suppliesArizona has joined Nevada in its legal battle against the Trump administration’s proposed cuts to their shares of the shrinking Colorado River.The move comes after the interior department announced restrictions this summer that could slash the water supplied to lower basin states – Arizona, California and Nevada – over the next two years depending on the river’s condition.Continue reading...

item.title: Hurricane Trudy strengthens to category 2 as it heads toward Mexico
item.author: Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Hurricane warning in effect from Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes as storm moves toward Pacific coastTrudy strengthened to a category 2 hurricane as it moved toward Mexico’s south-western and west-central Pacific coast on Saturday, the US National Hurricane Center said.A hurricane warning was in effect from Manzanillo in Colima state to Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco. The latest NHC data showed Trudy with maximum sustained winds of 100mph (155km/h) and about 205 miles (330km) south/south-east of Cabo Corrientes and 115 miles (180km) south/south-west of Manzanillo, moving north-west at 10mph (17km/h).Continue reading...

item.title: Two people, including child, killed after person drives through soccer game in Kansas
item.author: Guardian staff
item.content:encoded: The driver of the vehicle is in custody, and two juveniles were in the vehicle, according to Wichita police departmentTwo people, including a child, were killed during a soccer game in Wichita, Kansas, when a person drove a vehicle through the field at Stryker soccer complex, police have confirmed. Multiple other people were injured.The driver of the vehicle is in custody, Aaron Moses of the Wichita police department said Saturday in a news conference. There were two juveniles in the vehicle, he said.Continue reading...

item.title: NYC Subway Shooting in Midtown Leaves Man Dead
item.author: Maia Coleman and Wesley Parnell
item.content:encoded: The shooting occurred on Saturday at the 7th Avenue Station on 53rd Street, near Times Square. The Police Department said there have been no arrests.

item.title: New York City police seek suspect in fatal subway station shooting
item.author: Keely Aouga
item.content:encoded: Suspect shot a man in his 30s on the E train platform of the 53rd Street-7th Avenue subway station, according to NYPDA man was shot and killed in a New York City subway station Saturday afternoon, and the New York police department is searching for the suspect.The suspect fatally shot a man in his 30s on the E train platform of the 53rd Street-7th Avenue subway station, according to a statement from the NYPD.Continue reading...

item.title: After School Shooting in Bend, Ore., a Community Tries to Recapture Its Identity
item.author: Anna Griffin and Maia Spoto
item.content:encoded: Days after the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School, the community is questioning its resilience — and safety.

item.title: Unrest Mars Day of Protest in France, as Student Movement Turns National
item.author: Catherine Porter
item.content:encoded: Riots broke out in several French cities alongside peaceful marches of tens of thousands of people demonstrating against rising living costs and poor school conditions.

item.title: No action to be taken against wife of PM’s aide over Palestine Action post
item.author: Nadeem Badshah
item.content:encoded: Tweet by Sarah Helm, wife of national security adviser Jonathan Powell, ‘does not meet criminal threshold’No further action will be taken against Sarah Helm, the wife of the prime minister’s national security adviser, after she was accused of supporting the banned protest group Palestine Action.Continue reading...

item.title: ICE agent who crashed into man in Texas was targeting suspect who died years ago, family says
item.author: Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Federal officer slammed vehicle into a construction worker while pursuing a man who died in similar circumstancesA federal officer slammeda vehicle into a Houston construction worker and broke his leg, believing him to be a man who apparently died years ago, the dead man’s family said on Friday, further calling into question the account given by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).The worker, 48-year-old Miguel Parra Hernandez of Mexico, remains hospitalized with multiple leg fractures and needs reconstructive ankle surgery, according to FIEL, a Houston-based immigration advocacy group. At a news conference on Friday, the group said the alleged suspect’s family had shared documentation proving his death.Continue reading...

item.title: Reform candidate filmed saying asylum seekers should be put in ‘concentration camps’
item.author: Nadeem Badshah and agency
item.content:encoded: Would-be MP recorded telling undercover reporter in ITV investigation that Muslims could not be BritishA would-be Reform UK MP told an undercover reporter that Muslims could not be British and asylum seekers should be put in “concentration camps”.The comments were recorded as part of the undercover investigation by ITV that has already seen Reform accused of “appalling behaviour” and “extreme racism”.Continue reading...

item.title: Most NSW homes destroyed in black summer bushfires were within 100 metres of vegetation
item.author: Graham Readfearn Climate and environment correspondent
item.content:encoded: : Research confirms official advice about high-risk properties and warns worsening conditions will make more homes unsafeAlmost every home destroyed in New South Wales during the black summer bushfires of 2019-20 was inside the 100 metre buffer zone used to identify properties most at risk, new research has found.The findings are an endorsement of the risk maps used by authorities, but the research warns that as global heating generates ever-worsening fire conditions, firefighters may have to extend the recommended distances between homes and vegetation to keep properties safe.Continue reading...

item.title: Plover, not a fighter: protected bird 12th man on Tasmanian cricket ground as staff mow around nest
item.author: Ima Caldwell
item.content:encoded: While masked lapwings have a reputation for swooping during nesting season, Windsor Park oval’s resident plover just wants a good inningsAt Windsor Park in Riverside, just outside Launceston in northern Tasmania, a masked lapwing has claimed prime real estate in the middle of a community sports ground, showing complete indifference to the weekend cricket matches taking place around it.Warming a nest of eggs, the bird has been affectionately dubbed “Faf Swoop Plessis” by locals – a play on former South African cricket captain Faf du Plessis.Continue reading...

item.title: Israeli settlers attack European diplomats in West Bank
item.author: Emma Graham-Harrison in Taybeh
item.content:encoded: French mayor and archbishop also attacked during violent attempt to stop Palestinians harvesting olives Israeli settler militants have attacked European diplomats, a French mayor and the archbishop of Cambrai in Taybeh, in the occupied West Bank, injuring three people and damaging a car, in the latest violent attempt to prevent Palestinians from harvesting olives on their own land.Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries, was wearing his red, white and blue sash of office and attempting to enter a vehicle with diplomatic plates when he was assaulted and knocked to the ground on Saturday.Continue reading...

item.title: Weak Links Start to Show in A.I. Borrowing
item.author: Maureen Farrell and Rob Copeland
item.content:encoded: Debt trouble at CoreWeave, Oracle and SoftBank raises questions about whether there are broader problems with the data center build-out.

item.author: Maureen Dowd
item.content:encoded: The president’s crazy actions have Democrats on the cusp of victory — and they’ll be coming for him.

item.title: Revealed: French police used UK-funded 4x4 vehicles to charge student protesters
item.author: Diane Taylor
item.content:encoded: French government investigating why cars funded by UK to prevent asylum seekers crossing Channel were used in school protestsFrench police have used 4x4 vehicles paid for by British taxpayers to charge at student protesters during the school protests that have swept the country.The French government has confirmed that an investigation has been launched into why the cars, funded by the UK government specifically to prevent asylum seekers crossing the Channel, were used during a protest involving school students in Dunkirk.Continue reading...

item.title: Plaque telling story of African-Caribbean prisoners in Britain stolen within days
item.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
item.content:encoded: Descendants say theft from Portchester Castle reflects racism that has haunted ‘generation after generation’The theft of a plaque in Hampshire that told the little-known story of African-Caribbean prisoners in 18th-century Britain reflects the enduring racism that has fuelled centuries of atrocities against Black and Indigenous Caribbean people, their descendants say.Ronald Raymond McDonald, a professional drummer, was part of a delegation that travelled from Belize and elsewhere to Portchester Castle near Portsmouth last week to honour their ancestors: 2,500 men, women and children transported to Britain as prisoners of war in 1796.Continue reading...

item.title: SNP says campaign for next referendum on independence ‘has already begun’
item.author: Patrick Greenfield
item.content:encoded: John Swinney tells party conference SNP will use ‘six-figure war chest’ to renew argument for leaving UKJohn Swinney has said that the second referendum campaign for Scottish independence “has already begun”, revealing a nationwide effort to renew the argument for leaving the UK in his keynote address to the SNP party conference.On Saturday, the Scottish first minister said the SNP would launch its “most sophisticated campaign in history” to convince Scottish voters of the benefits of independence, backed by “a six-figure war chest”.Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s pause on Russia sanctions is ‘reward’ for Putin, Zelenskyy says
item.author: Andrew Roth in Kyiv
item.content:encoded: Ukrainian president warns it will embolden Russian leader and intensify war as Moscow hits country’s power plantsVolodymyr Zelenskyy has described Donald Trump’s decision to roll back sanctions on Russia as a “reward” for Vladimir Putin and warned it will embolden the Russian leader and intensify the Kremlin’s war, as Moscow launched one of its worst strikes yet on Ukraine’s power plants in an attempt to black out the country’s cities before winter.The Ukrainian president also said he expected the Trump administration to lift more sanctions against Russia in the future and called for Europe to establish its own negotiations with Moscow as the US has sought better ties and business deals with the Kremlin.Continue reading...

item.title: Pope Leo discharged from hospital after cancer operation
item.author: Angela Giuffrida in Rome
item.content:encoded: Doctors say pontiff is ‘fit for discharge’ after operation to remove cancerous tumour from his lungLeo, 71, was deemed “fit for discharge”, his doctors, Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora, said in a statement published by the Vatican.Continue reading...

item.title: Isabel Allende wins €1m Spanish literary prize under pseudonym
item.author: Emma Loffhagen and Ella Creamer
item.content:encoded: Chilean-American author awarded Premio Planeta for sequel to her 1982 debut novel, The House of the SpiritsThe Chilean-American author Isabel Allende has won Spain’s €1m (£843,000) Premio Planeta, one of the world’s most lucrative literary prizes, under a pseudonym, with a sequel to her celebrated debut novel, The House of the Spirits.Allende, 84, won the 75th edition of the award on Thursday with , which returns to the characters of her 1982 novel, a multigenerational family saga set against political upheaval in a country inspired by Chile.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We’re not playing games’: Parents launch playground protests to fight school field sell-off
item.author: Steven Morris
item.content:encoded: School looking to sell piece of open land beloved by people in Devon town to fund refurbishmentsOn Saturdays throughout autumn, residents of Totnes have met at a field on the banks of the River Dart to play ballgames, fly kites or simply sit on the grass and chat.But it hasn’t just been about having fun – this has been a “play protest” aimed at trying to save a beloved piece of open land in the historic Devon market town.Continue reading...

item.content:encoded: The longtime friends and creative partners on what U2 still means — and what would make them call it quits.

item.content:encoded: Campus rape investigations are often riddled with problems — but eliminating them would be much worse.

item.title: UAE agrees with Saudi Arabia to re-enter Yemen conflict amid Houthi gains
item.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
item.content:encoded: United Arab Emirates will reportedly resume payments to Yemeni forces as gains by Iran-backed Houthi fighters alarm Gulf state rulersThe United Arab Emirates has agreed to re-enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to some government forces fighting Iran-aligned Houthis in the south, according to sources in Yemen. In return, Saudi Arabia has agreed to provide air cover for the anti-Houthi force.Continue reading...

item.title: Corporate Tax Revenue Falls Even as Profits Soar Under Trump
item.author: Andrew Duehren
item.content:encoded: The annual decline was about $70 billion. Companies are writing off billions in A.I. investments, taking advantage of tax cuts that President Trump signed into law.

item.title: ‘I cannot carry all of this alone’: the couples kept apart by the war in Gaza
item.author: Aseel Mousa
item.content:encoded: Families have been scattered, fathers separated from their children, and couples unable to reunite and marryWijdan Abu Matar, 43, was forced to leave Gaza in November 2023 with her eight children for medical treatment, while her injured husband, Hatem, remained behind.Wijdan and her family were living in the Nuseirat refugee camp when the Gaza war began with the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack on Israel. Ten days later, on 17 October that year, an Israeli strike hit the al-Muhandseen tower, near their home, injuring Wijdan and every member of her family.Continue reading...

item.title: Mexican judge sentences three men to 158 years in prison for murders of Australian and US surfers​
item.author: Kat Wong with agencies
item.content:encoded: Australian ​brothers Jake ​and Callum Robinson, and ​their ‌American friend Carter Rhoad, were killed while on a surf trip in Baja California in 2024A Mexican ⁠judge ⁠has sentenced ​three men to 158 years ⁠and nine months in prison each for ⁠the murder of ​two Australian ‌brothers ‌and their American friend during ‌a 2024 surf trip to the state of Baja California.The ‌defendants were declared guilty a week ​ago of homicide, aggravated robbery, robbery with violence and vehicle theft ⁠with violence, crimes committed against ​Australian ​brothers Jake ​and Callum Robinson, and ​their ‌American friend ​Carter Rhoad.Continue reading...

item.title: Mimicking populists will not ease cost of living or boost productivity, Mathias Cormann warns
item.author: Kat Wong
item.content:encoded: Former minister and OECD head urges Australia not to adopt migration caps, with research showing migrants boost employmentAustralia’s mainstream political parties are being warned not to adopt populist policies such as migration caps to address voters’ grievances over the cost of living.Instead, Australia’s longest-serving finance minister, Mathias Cormann, is urging politicians to deliver housing, real wage growth and lower energy costs by boosting productivity.Continue reading...

item.title: Gone to the dogs: racing fans mourn closure of ‘Wenty’, Sydney’s historic greyhound track
item.author: Australian Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Thousands pack Wentworth Park for the final time before the stadium is demolished and returned to parklandThe end of an era has fallen upon an Australian sporting landmark as the greyhound races at an inner-city track kicked off for the very last time.Thousands packed into Wentworth Park in central Sydney on Friday night, where greyhound races have been held since 1932, for the last race meeting before the track’s planned demolition.Continue reading...

item.title: Brazilian Amazon deforestation falls to lowest on record as pivotal vote looms
item.author: Jonathan Watts
item.content:encoded: Forest clearance at smallest total since records began in 1988 in success for Lula ahead of presidential run-offDeforestation in the Brazilian Amazon has fallen to its lowest level since records began, new government data shows.But whether this globally important success is maintained or reversed is on a knife edge ahead of a presidential election run-off on 25 October between two candidates with sharply different visions for the future of the rainforest and how that affects relations with the US under Donald Trump.Continue reading...

item.title: No 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU scheme
item.author: Rowena Mason, Lisa O’Carroll and Jasper Jolly
item.content:encoded: Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe packageNo 10 has left the door open to imposing tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles as part of the Made in Europe package, prompting a warning from Beijing that such a move would be “discriminatory”.Continue reading...

item.title: Brazil’s Lula says he now backs lowering age of criminal responsibility to 16
item.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
item.content:encoded: Lula reverses position on age of responsibility for ‘heinous’ crimes in what many see as a desperate electoral gambitBrazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has announced that he now supports lowering the age of criminal responsibility for “heinous” crimes from 18 to 16, reversing a longstanding policy in what is widely seen as a desperate electoral gambit.The U-turn, which Lula announced during a Thursday night interview with TV Globo, comes with the presidential runoff in just over a week. The incumbent faces an uphill battle to overturn the first-round victory of his opponent, the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who remains slightly ahead at the polls.Continue reading...

item.title: Israeli settlers attack olive farmers and Washington Post journalist in West Bank
item.author: William Christou
item.content:encoded: Settlers hurl rocks at Palestinians and beat photographer Heidi Levine as part of yearly attacks to disrupt harvestIsraeli settlers have attacked Palestinians across the occupied West Bank in a coordinated movement to disrupt the annual olive harvest, burning cars and trees and injuring Palestinians and a Washington Post photographer.Masked settlers wielding clubs and other weapons attacked people attempting to harvest their olives in West Bank towns on Friday. Palestinian authorities said they recorded attacks in eight villages, and injuries among at least 20 people.Continue reading...

item.title: India’s Cockroach Janta party leader arrested amid crackdown on protests
item.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
item.content:encoded: Abhijeet Dipke was detained before planned anti-government demonstrations in DelhiThe leader of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) youth movement, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained by police on Friday and then later formally arrested as authorities cracked down on fresh anti-government protests in the Indian capital.Dipke was detained before a planned Friday evening demonstration he had called in central Delhi, urging supporters of the movement to come out and hold up the Indian flag.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Tough to watch, impossible to ignore’: reviewers on NAZA documentary
item.author: Sammy Gecsoyler
item.content:encoded: Film interviewing military insiders about mass killing of civilians in Gaza wins widespread praise around the worldCritics around the world have hailed the award-winning documentary NAZA as a “brilliant and harrowing” film that is “impossible to ignore”.NAZA, which is produced by the Guardian and details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza, was released in UK cinemas this week and will be shown in more than 50 countries. As well as its global cinema releases, NAZA will be available free on the Guardian’s website from late November.Continue reading...

item.title: Flash floods destroy villages in central Nepal
item.author: Matt Andrews and Ed Walton for MetDesk
item.content:encoded: Landslide blocks river and triggers downstream flooding, while summer temperatures persist in PortugalFlash floods have swept through Nepal’s central Gorkha district after a pre-dawn landslide on 11 October blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering severe downstream flooding. Two villages in the worst-affected Chumanubri rural municipality were reportedly destroyed, with homes, roads and bridges washed away. Part of a hydropower station was also damaged.After river levels surged from 2 metres to nearly 8.5 metres within hours, the national disaster risk reduction and management authority reported that 204 homes were damaged, and more than 650 people had been affected. More than 100 foreign trekkers were stranded in the popular hiking region. The floods come just two months after catastrophic flooding and landslides devastated parts of the country on the border with Tibet, leaving thousands dead or missing.Continue reading...

item.title: Museum releases historical photos of island where Amelia Earhart may have crashed
item.author: Oliver Holmes
item.content:encoded: Images from New Zealand aerial survey of Nikumaroro in 1938 offer new clues over aviator’s disappearanceA New Zealand museum has released nearly 50 photos from a 1938 aerial survey of the island where Amelia Earhart is believed to have crash-landed, offering amateur sleuths new evidence to scour for traces of the pioneering aviator and her plane.The black-and-white images were published by the Air Force Museum of New Zealand after renewed interest in one of the biggest mysteries of the 20th century, spurred by a US expedition to the Pacific atoll of Nikumaroro in search of new clues.Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Opening the lid of a horrible secret’: Jamaicans confront enslavement with taboo-busting stories on screen
item.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
item.content:encoded: As violent spirits are unleashed in Sky’s Possession, observers see confident creatives reclaiming the island’s narratives in a form of ‘cultural reparation’ A woman opens a 300‑year‑old box, unleashing a violent spirit – it is the spirit of colonialism and oppression roaring back to life. It is a pivotal scene in Sky’s supernatural series Possession and symbolises a wider shift in Jamaica’s film industry, where directors are increasingly using the landscape to tell Jamaican stories – including those that confront enslavement, trauma and historical memory.The series is about a biracial British lawyer who travels to Jamaica to investigate a multimillion-pound inheritance dispute, only to uncover a dark, vengeful spirit tied to the plantation’s brutal colonial past.Continue reading...

item.title: Revealed: VW, Ford and Tesla batteries linked to destructive deforestation of indigenous lands
item.author: Stefano Valentino in Sulawesi and Ajit Niranjan
item.content:encoded: Mines in supply chains of western carmakers linked to widespread deforestation of primary rainforest in nickel-rich lands inhabited by Tolaki people in IndonesiaVolkswagen, Ford and Tesla are among the electric carmakers whose batteries may contain nickel mined in indigenous woodlands plagued by deforestation, an analysis has found, highlighting the struggle to make vehicles that are free from environmental destruction.Corporate disclosures and trade flows from the last two years show mines in the battery supply chains of automotive giants are linked to the loss of trees in Sulawesi, a wildlife hotspot in Indonesia that houses the world’s largest nickel deposits. The metal is widely used in cathodes in car batteries because it boosts energy density and increases range.Continue reading...

item.title: Nicolás Maduro tells New York court new torture allegations are ‘false’
item.author: Associated Press
item.content:encoded: Rewritten indictment accuses ex-Venezuela president and wife Cilia Flores of leading campaign of tortureNicolás Maduro insisted on Thursday during an appearance in a New York court that torture allegations in a rewritten drug trafficking indictment against the deposed Venezuelan president and his wife were “false accusations”.Maduro, shackled at the ankles, was brought to court to face the new charges accusing the couple of leading a state-sponsored campaign of repression that tortured scores of victims, including three Americans.Continue reading...

item.title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
item.author: Kalyeena Makortoff
item.content:encoded: Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as potential interest rate hikes spook marketsAn accelerating sell-off of AI-linked shares has hit global markets, as fears over rising inflation and future interest rate hikes spooked traders already wary of the heavily indebted sector.South Korea’s benchmark Kospi 200index, which is heavily skewed towards the companies that make memory chips, fell more than 8% overnight to a six-month closing low, triggering circuit breakers that brought trading to a halt at various points.Continue reading...

item.author: Reuters in Islamabad
item.content:encoded: Another three pupils from al-Khair school in Peshawar in critical condition after search for survivorsAt least 34 schoolchildren and a female teacher have died after the roof of a school collapsed during morning classes in the northern Pakistani city ⁠of Peshawar.As panicked parents ​and relatives thronged the site of the privately run al-Khair school to search for their loved ones, rescue workers spent hours pulling children from the rubble.Continue reading...

item.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
item.author: Sarah Johnson
item.content:encoded: At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reportsMass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report.More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, according to HIV Justice Network, an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.Continue reading...

item.title: Indonesia fights fire with dry ice as toxic haze spreads across region
item.author: Kate Lamb and agencies
item.content:encoded: Having tried cloud seeding and water bombing, one pilot project will see dry ice dispersed by plane across the province of South SumatraAs fires ravage Indonesia, emitting a toxic smoke that has drawn the ire of regional neighbours, the government is testing an unusual new approach to tackle the haze: dry ice.Having tried cloud seeding, water bombing and sending in army personnel to fight the fires, Indonesia’s coordinating security minister said dry ice would be dropped on the province of South Sumatra on Thursday.Continue reading...
